newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Eurobourses fall, rattled by Wall Street.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Eurobourses fall, rattled by Wall Street.

text.p: European bourses fell sharply on Wednesday as Wall Street made a poor opening a day after U.S. stocks tumbled to their biggest loss in five months.
On currency markets, the dollar weakened after its rally to a 23-month peak against the mark on Tuesday. Sterling also fell amid fears that its recent strength could harm British industry.
The losses on European bourses ended a record-breaking pace on much of the continent this week fuelled by investors who saw the recent strength of the dollar as a boon to exporters.

London and Paris shares were well down in mid-afternoon as Wall Street fell 0.3 precent at its opening, a follow-on from the wave of profit-taking on Tuesday which wiped 1.21 percent off the Dow Jones industrial average.
Frankfurt, which closed before Wall Street's opening, was showing a loss of 0.72 percent at the end of the session after hitting a record close of 2,886.98 points on Tuesday.

European bourses had been depressed by Tuesday's big fall on Wall Street. Big computer-driven sell programs in New York kicked in during a frantic last 10 minutes of trading to lock in profits after the Dow rose 500 points, or eight percent, in November.
"We haven't been following Wall Street up...we have been following it down...but I don't think it will be a disaster by any means," said a dealer in London.
But the gloom in London, where stocks fell 0.44 percent, was slightly offset by the the weaker pound which was seen as helping the exporting sector.
"Sterling is an important factor. If it weakens, it will help a lot of major stocks. So there are other things at work here besides Wall Street," the dealer said.
French stocks took the biggest knock from Wall Street, sliding 1.7 percent after a strong performance this week.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index was down to 2306.79 points at one stage. Alcatel Alsthom fell 3.2 percent to 459.8 francs following news that the government has suspended the Thomson SA privatisation.
Frankfurt closed down 0.7 percent, sapped by Wall Street's fall and the weaker dollar, after a day of quiet trading.
"It's consolidation today," said one traderin Frankfurt.
The dollar's slide hit exporting chemical and auto stocks. BMW, Hoechst and BASF were all lower after surging on Tuesday.
The dollar, a major factor in the price of German exports, edged lower against the mark after German economic growth in the third quarter exceeded most expectations.
The U.S. currency slid by a pfennig in early European trading as the dollar took a breather after its record-breaking pace. It recovered somewhat in later trading.
"It had a very solid run and things are settling down. The currencies are pausing for breath after yesterday's massive move," said David Bloom, currency strategist at HSBC James Capel.

Dollar was at 1.5605 marks in late morning, from 1.5647 on Tuesday, with the German currency drawing strength from figures showing Germany's economy expanded by one percent in the third quarter after a 1.5 percent increase in the previous quarter.

"They are pretty robust figures on the whole. After a very strong second-quarter the economy seems to be doing very well. It is definitely accelerating back to trend," said Klaus Baader, senior currency strategist at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell.
While the dollar weakened on profit-taking against the mark, yen, French franc and Swiss franc, attention switched to sterling which fell to $1.6385 from $1.6520 late on Tuesday.
"We needed a good bout of profit-taking...Everyone went for the exit together," said the trader.

The pound's slide from four-year highs started on Tuesday when Finance Minister Kenneth Clarke said industry was starting to fret about the pound's exchange rate. Businessmen are worried that sterling's rally might damage British competitiveness by making exports more expensive.
CURRENCIES AT 1545 GMT
The dollar was quoted at 113.17 yen and 1.5624 marks against 113.68 yen and 1.5647 marks in late Europe on Friday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1545 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE 100 index of leading British shares was down 18.1 points at 4,043.4.
PARIS - The CAC-40 share index was down 41.18 points at 2,307.93.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index closed down 20.91 points at 2,866..07.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold fixed in the afternoon at $370.90, compared to the close on Tuesday of $$367.85. Silver was at $4.82, up 11 cents.
